Beyond the drawing office

Beyond my professional engineering work, I am a deeply practical person and I love DIY. I take pride in performing all the regular maintenance on my car — from oil and coolant changes to replacing brake rotors, pads and electrical components — and I once successfully replaced the starter motor.

That passion extends to cycling. I recently custom-built a carbon-fibre gravel bike from the frame to the gears, personally sourcing and assembling every component for peak performance aligned to my preferences. I also converted my mountain bike into an electric bicycle — after taking the safety measures into account.

Whether I am out on a multi-day bikepacking trip or keeping to my daily fitness routine, I am driven by the same curiosity and attention to detail that I bring to structural engineering. For me, these hobbies are more than leisure — they are an extension of my engineering mindset.

Technical expertise

Structural analysis & design

Global & local strength, fatigue, vibration, harmonic and buckling FEA — closed with design optimization that feeds the construction model.

Structure modelling for FEA — Modelling the whole ship structure for global analysis, as well as building the sub-models used for local FEA.

Global strength FEA — Global strength analysis in the functional design phase for two icebreakers. I studied the global strength of the ship hull girder considering the global vertical wave bending moment, horizontal wave bending moment, still-water bending moment and dynamic wave loads, approved by the corresponding class society. I developed an in-house app to apply the dynamic wave loads in ANSYS and visualize them, and wrote, with the help of AI, scripts for load application, boundary condition definition and result extraction — plus post-processing scripts to make sure the results match the applied loads.

Fatigue assessment — Responsible for global and local fatigue assessment, and for optimizing the most fatigue-critical areas, on two major projects — the Canadian polar icebreaker and the German Polarstern icebreaker. I combined FEA with manual calculations and customized a fatigue analysis method for icebreakers based on IACS rules. I also developed a parametric Excel sheet for fatigue and strength assessment and verification, to ease and automate future calculations for similar icebreaker projects.

Local FEA — Dozens of local FE analyses: engine foundations, double-bottom structure, crane foundations (deck crane, boat crane and A-crane), engine casing and reactor supports, masts, emergency genset foundations, working decks, fall-arrest anchors, moon pool, and welding strength FE analysis. In some cases the global loads are carried into the local model as boundary conditions.

Ship dynamics and offshore structures — Strength FEA of offshore structures and ships after mapping the dynamic loads — from waves, mooring, towing and similar — onto the wetted surface. I dived deeper into this during my master’s degree at Aalto University with hydroelasticity analysis. I have both industrial and academic experience in this field.

Global & local vibration FEA — Optimized the vibration performance of a mast structure in the functional and detailed design phases by changing its shape, dimensions and stiffness to carry the specified loads without exceeding the vibration criteria or resonating with machinery and propulsion excitation frequencies. Also studied the eigenmodes of different structural details across the ship and stiffened them accordingly. I have also obtained the eigenmodes of the global ship hull girder in air and in water by two methods — modal analysis and acoustic analysis.

Local harmonic analysis — Harmonic analyses to predict accelerations at specific locations in the ship against the different criteria — structural safety and the comfort of passengers and crew.

Buckling analysis — FEA & hand calculations — Alongside the local FEA work, I studied the buckling performance of structures under various compression loads, verified with hand calculations.

Nonlinear FEA — I have mainly considered geometric and material nonlinear FEA in academic research — for example, studying the ultimate bending moment amidship and comparing it against the plastic grounding load.

Design optimization and automation — Runs through everything above: I revise the current structure, optimize it to meet the criteria, and update the drawings so my structural design colleagues can apply the changes in the construction modeling software (CADMATIC). I have also developed apps and codes for colleagues to use — among them the grating selector tool — and provided the structure designers with straightforward guides for determining the maximum opening size allowed in girders without returning to the structural team. The guides are based on the linear response and the type of load on the deck above the opening to be cut.

Naval architecture & stability

Intact & damaged stability — Stability assessment for concept designs and for heavy-lifting project loading scenarios.

  • Compartment modelling and definition of watertight doors, ventilation openings, evacuation routes, doors, compartment connections, windows and similar for the intact and damage stability assessment.
  • The tasks include producing the tank plan drawing, adding or removing tank connections and openings, and changing compartment sizes when necessary. Also, in some projects I modelled a parametric hull for fairing and optimization.
  • For heavy-lifting projects — studying the loading scenarios step by step to ensure the loads and stability stay within the criteria limits.
  • Projects: Capesize bulk carrier, VLCC, double-ended ferry, RoPax, deck carrier and more.

Hull girder scantling & class rules — Scantling and strength assessment with class software.

General arrangement design — GA design for concept ships, developed hand in hand with the stability work.

Launching & marine operations — Ship launching and pulling-up scenarios using marine airbags.

Ship dynamics & hydrodynamics

Wave loads & seakeeping — Global wave bending moment and shear force using 3D potential flow theory in AQWA, and with NAPA, Maxsurf and HydroSTAR. RAOs and motions of ships and offshore structures. Structure response in the frequency domain and the time domain.

Powering — Holtrop method and manual calculation.

Hydroelasticity — Wetted modal analysis and elastic response with HydroSTAR and Homer, and calculating hydroelastic loads.

Mooring & towing loads — Mapping mooring and towing dynamic loads onto the wetted surface, plus studying the motions and responses.

CFD — Flow and resistance studies with Fluent and ICEM CFD — basic knowledge.

AI-assisted coding for marine tasks (EXPANDING)

AI-assisted coding — Dart, Python, C++, HTML — I build software with AI-assisted coding in Dart, Python, C++ and HTML. I have built in-house apps that automate calculations and let other designers work independently without waiting on the busy structural team — among them a grating selector tool that calculates the best-fit grating size to carry a specified load. I have also built and published two applications on the Microsoft Store: DayBook and Finnish Tutor. I also write ANSYS commands for faster load application, boundary condition definition, and extracting and visualising the results.

Excel — Several parametric Excel sheets and macros that automate repeatable calculations — among them a parametric fatigue and strength verification sheet for icebreaker projects.

MATLAB — Used in my master’s thesis and some of my publications for spectral fatigue analysis — back in 2018, before AI coding, I wrote several pages of code to perform the sophisticated spectral fatigue calculations.
